stage: domain M / domain E interface, step 10 (bridge testing) and step 12 (falsifiers)
failed_output: A leave-one-out geographic measurement over attested Dravidian languages was interpreted as showing something about where Dravidian was spoken, and specifically as making Brahui's northwestern position anomalous and in need of a migration explanation. Recorded in full at DMB-001.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure. A delete-one statistic computed over a set with one extreme member measures the influence of that member on the statistic. Reporting the remainder is a sensitivity report about the instrument. Converting it into a claim about a language family's geography is the step-10 bridge failure in its exact form: the link from 'the statistic moves a long way when this element is deleted' to 'this element is anomalous in the history' is a separate claim and was never made, let alone tested.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: It assumes that the set of attested Dravidian languages is a sample of Dravidian geography. It is a sample of survival. The languages attested today are the ones that were not replaced, and the archive that records them is the colonial and post-colonial survey record, which enumerated speech communities it reached and classified. Deleting Brahui does not simulate a Dravidian world without Brahui; it simulates the record we would hold if one more replacement had run to completion. Under the step-6 archive audit that is the whole question, and the statistic assumes it away.
affected_claims: DMB-001 (superseded), DMB-002 (restatement); bears on IH-135 / hypothesis H-01, IH-031, IH-156 / rejected row R-10; and on the reading of DME-022 and DME-023
correction: DMB-001 is SUPERSEDED and retained, not deleted. DMB-002 restates the claim to the two things the statistic can carry: the instrument's exposure to one datapoint, and the size of the gap between Brahui and the next-nearest attested Dravidian language. Unit 2 supplies the arithmetic (DMB-010 to DMB-013) by computing the delete-one influence of all twenty attested varieties, so that Brahui's influence is reported against a distribution rather than on its own.
future_control: No leave-one-out, jackknife or delete-one statistic in this repository is reported without (a) the per-element influence of every element, not only the element of interest, and (b) an explicit statement of the reference point or estimand and of who chose it. A delete-one result reported for one element alone is a sensitivity claim presented as a finding.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: The reading of DME-022 and DME-023 as bearing on donor-language geography. Those rows are corpus-internal and correctly scoped, but DME-023 states a compatibility with 'the greater Indus and north-west' whose own geographic reference point is not stated numerically. stage: domain M, step 4 (evidence classes kept separate) and step 10 (bridge testing)
topic: North Dravidian subgrouping and the independence assumption
failed_output: A Euclidean distance from each attested Dravidian language to a northwestern reference point, with the languages treated as independent observations and Brahui read off as an isolated outlier.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure with a bias consequence. A distance-to-reference statistic has no term for shared descent, so it cannot represent a clade. If Brahui, Kurukh and Malto subgroup, their three positions are not three observations; they are one observation of an ancestor's location plus whatever happened afterwards. Treating them as three both inflates the apparent support and makes Brahui look like it stands alone when it may be the northwestern member of a group that also reaches Jharkhand. A second and separate defect: Euclidean distance over a latitude/longitude pair is not a distance on the earth, and its error is a function of latitude, which is exactly the axis the northwest/south contrast runs along.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: The representation is not neutral. Rendering a language family as a scatter of points in a plane is the representation in which 'Brahui stands alone' is true by construction, because the representation has deleted the only structure - descent - that could make it not stand alone. Choosing that representation and then reading a historical verdict out of it is a case of the instrument supplying the conclusion. The pull is bidirectional and must be named as such: an isolated northwestern outlier can be talked up as a relict of an early northwestern distribution, or talked up as a recent arrival. Neither follows from the scatter, and the prestige-bias and preferred-counter-narrative tests both bite here.
affected_claims: DMB-001 (superseded), DMB-005; and every claim that treats Brahui's position as evidence in either direction, including IH-135 / H-01
correction: Unit 2 measures the thing the statistic could not see. Exclusive cognate sharing across Brahui, Kurukh and Malto is computed from a retrieved cognate-coded Dravidian dataset (SRC-049) and reported against every other pair and triple in the same dataset (DMB-017 to DMB-022), so the subgroup is measured rather than assumed. The contested status of the subgroup is recorded separately at DMB-023 to DMB-026 rather than folded into the measurement.
future_control: Any measurement over two or more languages in this repository states, in the claim row itself, whether it assumes the languages are independent observations, and if the languages are claimed to be related it names the tree it assumed or records that it used none. Any planar distance over geographic coordinates reports the great-circle distance alongside it, or is not reported.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: The same reaudit targets as BF-005: RA-004 for DME-023's unstated geographic reference, RA-005 for the inherited Brahui rows. Additionally, no earlier work in this repository has ever used a phylogenetic assumption, so there is no prior tree-based claim to reaudit; that absence is itself why the control above is written as a positive requirement rather than a correction.

stage: Extraction and counting, pur- 4J corpus unit, 2026-09-07
topic: Whether a numeral in a Rigvedic stanza counts the fort word
failed_output: A mechanical numeral-noun agreement test scored on case, gender and number, which returned PARTIAL for navati- 'ninety' and would have excluded five of the six passages stating ninety-nine forts.
bias_or_method_failure: Deference to the reproducible instrument over the reading. The test was scriptable, auditable and wrong: navati- is a feminine SINGULAR collective ('a ninety') governing a plural puraḥ, so it agrees in case and gender and never in number. Following the instrument would have produced a tidy, re-runnable, false result — and one that happened to minimise the ninety-nine, which is also the direction of this project's available soft landing.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: Machine-checkable output carries more institutional prestige here than a philological judgement, because this repository's whole design privileges reproducibility. That is right as a default and wrong in this instance, and the design does not by itself flag the exception.
affected_claims: PUR4J-004; PUR4J-005; PUR4J-I-01; every COUNTS-PUR verdict on a navati- row in 03-REGISTERS/rigveda-pur-counts.csv

future_control: Any mechanical agreement test over Vedic morphology must be checked against collective and governing numerals before its output is used. More generally: when an instrument and a reading disagree, the register carries both columns rather than the winner.

stage: Interpretation, pur- 4J corpus unit, 2026-09-07
topic: Whether the Rigvedic fort counts are formulaic
failed_output: PUR4J-007 as first written: 'Sambara's forts are counted at ninety, ninety-nine, one hundred, the hundredth and hundreds across six passages. Every count value the constitution section 4J enumerates attaches to this one opponent.' It was VERIFIED and it was the strongest of the four diagnostics behind PUR4J-I-01.
bias_or_method_failure: PREFERRED-COUNTER-NARRATIVE FAILURE, caught by the independent reviewer and not by this unit's own section 8.2 test. Three of the five values were wrong, and all three errors ran the same way — toward the deflationary conclusion that the counts are formulaic. (1) RV 1.130.7's ninety are broken FOR Puru and Divodasa, datives; Sambara stands in a separate clause with no genitive attaching the forts to him. The row rested on Sambara merely occurring in the stanza — the exact inference PUR4J-006 and the counts register's own note declare invalid, in the same unit. (2) 'The hundredth' had already been withdrawn as a fort count by this branch's own COUNTS-SERIES-COMPLETION fix, which reworded three other claims and missed this one. (3) 'Hundreds' at RV 6.31.4 was a misreading of satani against three unanimous translators and against this register's own treatment of the identical form at RV 1.53.8.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: Not archival. The pull is that instability is the interesting result: a count that varies is evidence for formula, and the unit had already named formulaicity as its available soft landing and built four controls against adopting it. Three of those controls held. The one that failed is the one that interrogated the CONCLUSION rather than re-deriving the EVIDENCE, which is the specific weakness of an adversarial test run by the author.
affected_claims: PUR4J-007 (restated, demoted to PROVISIONAL); PUR4J-002, PUR4J-003 and PUR4J-009 (the 'hundreds' member removed; 100 now stated in 9 passages, not 8); PUR4J-I-01 diagnostic prediction 1 (restated from FAILS to INCONCLUSIVE)
correction: PUR4J-007 now claims only what survives: ninety-nine in three passages and one hundred in two, five passages and two values, and those two values are the pair PUR4J-008 argues are one schema. PUR4J-I-01's prediction 1 is downgraded to INCONCLUSIVE and the interpretation's support is restated as two clear diagnostics of four rather than three.
future_control: An author-run adversarial test must re-derive its own load-bearing evidence from the text, not interrogate the conclusion drawn from it. Concretely: any claim of the form 'value X attaches to entity Y' must cite the syntax that attaches them — a genitive, an agreement, a governing numeral — and never stanza co-occurrence, in a unit that has itself proved co-occurrence invalid.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: None outside this unit. Within it, every claim citing PUR4J-007 was traced and restated; PUR4J-I-01 is the only interpretation affected.

correction: All four targets are now screened and the non-toponymic uses are kept in the register as their own classifications rather than dropped, so they stay auditable. DRM-007 now states the measured figures for all four.
future_control: A screen applied to one member of a set is applied to all of them before any claim generalises across the set.

stage: step 3, geography; found by adversarial review
failed_output: DRM-010 stated that every findspot for the four toponyms is Mesopotamian, Syrian or Assyrian, and named Iran among the regions where no such text was found. Three Old Akkadian texts in the unit's own register are from Susa, which is in Iran; one is from Alalakh, in modern Turkey; and 71 of the texts have no findspot at all.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE. The claim was read off a frequency table's top rows rather than derived from the full distribution, and it was stated with a universal quantifier - 'every' - that the register it cited refutes in four rows. It was called 'the decisive geographical result' in the method note and stated flatly in public copy.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That the head of a frequency distribution is the distribution. Fifteen rows of a Counter.most_common() do not license a statement about all of it.
affected_claims: DRM-010, DR-NEG-001, APA-R-001, HYP-R-006's geographical gate, and the draft copy's note on the four names.
correction: Restated with its exceptions and its base: 720 of 791 texts have a findspot, 716 of those are Mesopotamian, Syrian or Assyrian, and the four exceptions are named by P-number. The narrower point survives and is the one that governs the domain.
future_control: No claim quantified over a distribution may be written from a truncated frequency table. The tail is checked, and any universal quantifier is derived explicitly.

stage: step 13 and step 5; found by adversarial review
failed_output: DRM-026 called all occurrences of eme-bal / eme-bala 'the interpreter title', counted 25 of them from an uncommitted grep, and called Marhashi 'best-attested' among what were three single occurrences.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE. The one measurement in the unit carrying an argument about LANGUAGE was the one produced outside the committed pipeline, so no reader could re-derive it; several occurrences are boats, flour and jars rather than a title; and one is a lexical equation glossing the sequence with Akkadian, which the unit did not engage at all. MISDIAGNOSIS CORRECTED 2026-09-09 after re-review: the first version of this row said 'the count was of grep LINES rather than occurrences'. That is not what happened - the original grep used -o and did count occurrences. The undercount, 25 against 31, is caused by ATF damage markup INSIDE the sequence - eme#-bala, eme#-[bala], [eme]-bala#, eme-[bala-me], eme-bala#-[me] - which a literal string match cannot see and which the pipeline's bare() strips before matching. That is a general hazard: ANY unnormalised search over this corpus undercounts damaged tokens, and it is not confined to this term.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That a term is what its best-known instance is. eme-bala in an administrative list beside a jar is not obviously the same word as eme-bala in an official's title, and the unit assumed it was.
correction: eme-bal is now a target in the extraction script with its own classifier and five classifications. The measurement is 31 occurrences in 26 texts, of which 4 stand beside a named region - two Marhashi, one Martu, one Gutium. The claim was rewritten to what those figures support.
future_control: Any measurement that carries an argument goes through the committed pipeline, with its exclusions written out, before it is written into a claim. No exceptions for a quick check that turns out to be interesting. And, separately: no search over this corpus is run on raw text. ATF markup is stripped before matching, or the count silently excludes every damaged occurrence - which are exactly the occurrences a philologist would most want to see.

stage: step 7, hypothesis gating; found by adversarial review
failed_output: HYP-R-007 failed the identification partly on a chronological gate that asserted, with no retrieval and with the row's own source_dependencies reading 'None - there is no source to depend on', that Mehrgarh's principal occupation ends well before the period in which Marhashi is attested.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE, and the same one BF-031 records this unit refusing an hour earlier for the Ajanta date. The difference is the direction: refusing to correct Ajanta cost the unit a tidy conclusion, while asserting Mehrgarh's dates bought one - the destruction of a trap the owner had named. Unretrieved knowledge was admitted where it was congenial and excluded where it was not.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That a fact one is confident of is a fact one has. The gate exists to stop exactly that substitution.
affected_claims: HYP-R-007, and DRM-018 by association, though DRM-018's own reasoning does not depend on the withdrawn sentence.
correction: The dating sentence is withdrawn and the row now fails the identification on the absence of positive evidence and of any proposing source, which is sufficient and is sourced. Neither row now says anything about where Marhashi was or when Mehrgarh was occupied.
future_control: Every gate verdict states which of its grounds are retrieved. A gate that fails a hypothesis on an unretrieved ground is not a gate.

stage: step 4 and step 7; found by adversarial review
failed_output: The museum-candidate register put agate and chalcedony into a class called LOOK-ALIKE-CONTROL, alongside glass, faience and Egyptian blue, and the draft copy presented all 425 as objects that are not the target materials.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE. DRR-009, in this unit's own claim register, states that bead carnelian IS heat-treated iron-rich agate. So the control set contained the target material, and an object catalogued 'agate' and one catalogued 'carnelian' may be the same mineral differing only in a cataloguer's word - which is the register's own thesis about attribution, applied everywhere except to its own class boundaries.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That a catalogue's material vocabulary carves at mineralogical joints. It does not: it carves at the joints of a cataloguing tradition.
affected_claims: DRM-021, DR-NEG-003, and the draft copy's blue-object sentence.
correction: The class is split. 285 lapis-attributed, 86 carnelian-attributed, 223 SAME-MINERAL-FAMILY (agate, chalcedony, sard), 202 LOOK-ALIKE-CONTROL (glass, faience, Egyptian blue, frit, azurite, turquoise, sodalite, jasper). The draft copy sentence is rewritten. The class was also documented as containing 'sard', which it cannot: CAR matches sard first, so that branch was dead code and the stated composition was one the data could not have. Corrected.
future_control: Before a control set is used as a control, check that it excludes the target material under every name the source uses for it.

stage: step 7, the translation standard; found by adversarial review
topic: Eight terms named as needing original-language work, none given it
failed_output: The method note's step 1 names me-luh-ha, ma2-gan, dilmun/ni-tuk, mar-ha-szi, za-gin3/uqnu, gug/samtu and eme-bal/eme-bala as terms needing original-language work. No register produced the constitution's ten fields for any of them, although the repository has precedent for doing so.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE, and it is upstream of several others. English renderings were doing argumentative work with no record behind them - 'interpreter' for eme-bal, 'village' for e2-duru5, 'unit of account' for gin2 dilmun, 'son of' for dumu - and BR-R-008 states the principle that a commodity label is not a mineral identification while no register implemented it.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That transliterating a word is the same as auditing the English category used to render it. The constitution separates these because the translation is where the historical question gets decided.
correction: 03-REGISTERS/domain-r-translation-fields.csv, covering the six consequential terms with the fields the standard specifies, and stating for each what the interpretive consequence of the alternative rendering would be. The inherited-category audit for 'civilisation' is recorded there too. EXTENDED 2026-09-09 after re-review: the first version covered six terms and excluded the four toponyms on the unargued ground that they were not 'the six consequential ones' - a self-assessment by the unit whose claims depend on them. TR-R-008 to TR-R-011 now cover me-luh-ha, ma2-gan, dilmun and mar-ha-szi. See BF-042.
future_control: A term named in step 1 as needing original-language work gets a translation-fields row before any claim uses its English rendering.

stage: the repair itself
failed_output: Moving the toponym-presence test to the top of cls_dilmun, as part of repairing BF-032, dropped the case-insensitive flag. 216 occurrences written DILMUN or GIN2-DILMUN in Akkadian logographic spelling were rejected as 'not the toponym' at a stroke, and the Dilmun text count fell to 281.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE INTRODUCED BY A REPAIR. Reordering a classifier's branches is not a neutral edit: a test written to run after a case-normalising step behaves differently when it runs before one. The fault was visible within a single run only because the rejected file is published and its Dilmun count jumped from 76 to 292.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That a repair is safer than the code it replaces. It is new code.
affected_claims: DRM-006, DRM-009, DRM-010, DRM-015, DR-NEG-001, APA-R-001, HYP-R-006 - all re-derived again. Final figures: 854 texts naming one of the four, 805 naming exactly one, 893 Dilmun occurrences.
correction: The regex now carries re.I with a comment saying why. Every classifier repair is followed by a diff of the REJECTED counts as well as the accepted ones.
future_control: Watch the rejected file, not only the register. A repair that silently moves occurrences into rejection looks like a cleaner result.

stage: step 4; found by re-review
failed_output: DRM-007 counted mes-me-luh-ha as a use of the Meluhha toponym and {gesz}mes-ma2-kan-na as NOT a use of the Magan toponym, three clauses apart in the same claim. They are the same formation - a toponym qualifying a timber - on two different names. The inconsistency had reached public copy, where 115 Magan-timber occurrences were offered as a parallel to Meluhha's polysemy without saying that 103 of them are Neo-Assyrian occurrences of one word.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE. The classifiers were written name by name and their category boundaries were never compared with one another, so a class that existed for one target had no counterpart for the next.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That a per-target classifier can be written per target. The categories are the analysis, and they have to be one scheme.
affected_claims: DRM-007 and the draft copy's note on the four names.
correction: One rule, in a named function material_or_creature(), applied to all four toponyms, with uniform classification strings: a toponym qualifying a material or a creature is not the toponym naming a place, whether or not the determinative is written.
future_control: Classification schemes are defined once for a set of targets and diffed across them before any claim generalises.

stage: step 4; found by re-review
topic: The determinative screen applied to four of six targets
failed_output: BF-033's repair extended the non-toponymic determinative screen to the four toponyms and not to the two stones, although the unit's own new translation register (TR-R-005) states that za-gin3 takes {sig2}, {siki}, {u2} and {d}. Twenty of the 844 occurrences classified 'carries no determinative at all' carried one - ten of them {d}, a divine name.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE, and a repeat of the one it repaired. BF-033's own future_control reads: 'A screen applied to one member of a set is applied to all of them before any claim generalises across the set.' The set is six targets. The control was written and then applied to four of them within the same repair.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That the members of a set are the ones currently in view. The stones were not in view because the finding that prompted the repair was about toponyms.
correction: cls_lapis and cls_carnelian now carry the same screen. 34 lapis occurrences and 2 carnelian occurrences move into a NON-STONE DETERMINATIVE class; DRB-019 restated as 824 unmarked, 630 stone, 64 logogram, 34 non-stone.

stage: step 7, the translation standard; found by re-review
failed_output: BF-038's repair produced translation-fields rows for six terms and excluded the four toponyms - me-luh-ha, ma2-gan, dilmun, mar-ha-szi - with the method note disposing of the gap in three words: 'the six consequential ones'.
bias_or_method_failure: METHOD FAILURE. The four excluded terms are the domain's central vocabulary and the ones DRM-007, DRM-008, DRM-018 and three hypothesis rows all turn on. 'Consequential' was assessed by the unit whose claims depend on them, without argument, in the direction of not doing the work.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That the terms needing the ten fields are the ones whose translation looks contestable. A toponym left untranslated still carries an identification, and the identification is exactly what the standard exists to keep separate from the word.
correction: TR-R-008 to TR-R-011 written. Each records that the unit leaves the toponym untranslated and states the interpretive consequence of the identification that would otherwise substitute for a translation - which for Marhashi is that the unit cannot place it at all.
